meta: A hermit by a dam, a kneeling pilgrim and a peasant woman in Antonio Francesco Peruzzini's landscape of about 1690.
about: A hermit sits by a dam in a river, with a skull and wooden crosses nailed to a tree behind him. A pilgrim kneels at the water's edge in the foreground, and across the water a peasant woman stands with a basket on her arm. Behind the trees a farm sits by a ruined tower in scaffolding, and an ancient temple stands far off at the right. Antonio Francesco Peruzzini painted it as a pendant to another picture in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Two horses start a race in an army camp before soldiers and civilians in Joseph Moerenhout's The Horse Race, 1829.
about: The start of a race between two horses takes place in an army camp, watched by soldiers and civilians. Joseph Moerenhout painted The Horse Race in 1829, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: William I, King of the Netherlands, in Joseph Paelinck's portrait of 1819, when he ruled a kingdom that included Belgium and Luxembourg.
about: Joseph Paelinck, a Belgian artist, painted this portrait of William I in 1819, when William ruled a united kingdom of the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg. After a long exile he had returned in 1813, near the end of the Napoleonic Wars, and the Congress of Vienna made him king the next year. The Belgian Revolution of 1830 cost him the southern part of his kingdom.

meta: Herdsmen rest with a dog, cows and sheep below a hill with a ruin in Gijsbert Gillisz de Hondecoeter's landscape of 1652.
about: A hilly landscape with herdsmen has a hill with a ruin on its top at the right. In the left foreground a herdsman and a herdswoman rest with a dog, cows and sheep. Rocks and trees stand at the foot of the hill on the right, and a lower plain lies far off at the left. Gijsbert Gillisz de Hondecoeter signed and dated it 1652 on a boulder at lower right.

meta: A Mughal prince visits a Sufi holy man in his cave, a painting by Govardhan of about 1630, reused in the Late Shah Jahan Album.
about: A Mughal prince visits a Sufi holy man in his cave dwelling. Most paintings in the Late Shah Jahan Album were made for it, but some older finished works were taken from their first mounts and set into the new borders, and this is one of them. The museum thinks it was chosen because it stresses the place of religion in Mughal life. The conch on the ground before the ascetic is blown at the start of prayer. Govardhan painted it around 1630.
credit_line: Andrew R. and Martha Holden Jennings Fund

meta: An imagined town square with Gothic buildings, a cathedral and an ox cart, painted by Kasparus Karsen about 1840.
about: This is an imagined townscape with Gothic buildings and a cathedral on a square. An ox cart stands in the street at the right. Kasparus Karsen painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1840.

meta: Christ's dead body hangs on the cross in Marco Pino's painting of about 1568 to 1570, with the Virgin, Saint John and Saint Catherine of Siena.
about: Against an open, hilly landscape the lifeless body of Christ hangs from a wooden cross, and his slumped head, open mouth and tense muscles catch the drama of the moment of his death. The monumental figures of the Virgin on the left and Saint John the Evangelist stand beside the cross, and Saint Catherine of Siena adores him. Marco Pino painted it on panel between 1568 and 1570.

meta: Prince Frederik Hendrik on horseback before fortifications, trenches and marching armies, painted by Pauwels van Hillegaert in 1629.
about: Prince Frederik Hendrik rides a horse in front of a background of fortifications, trenches and advancing armies. Pauwels van Hillegaert painted the portrait, which the catalog dates to 1629. The Rijksmuseum holds it and says no more about the scene. The Rijksmuseum holds it and says no more about the scene.

meta: Bertrand Du Guesclin reveals who he is after beating everyone in a tournament, in Pierre Révoil's painting of 1812.
about: The Tournament shows the last moments of a legend about Bertrand Du Guesclin, who competed anonymously in a tournament, beat all comers and then revealed his identity. Pierre Révoil painted it in 1812 and gave it to the Museum of Fine Arts in Lyon, which still owns it, some time before 1815.

meta: Pan Lang rides backward on a donkey for a last look at Mount Hua, from a pair of screens by Unkoku Tōgan, early 1600s.
about: This is one of a pair of screens showing episodes from the stories of two famed officials and poets who were banished by their rulers, Su Shi of the 1000s and Pan Lang of the 900s. Su Shi's comments on economic reforms were taken as criticism of the emperor, and Pan Lang wrote an ill-advised verse about one of the king's horses. Here Pan rides backward on his donkey as he returns from exile, so that he can look once more at his now beloved Mount Hua. Unkoku Tōgan painted the screens in the early 1600s.

meta: A Manchurian nobleman and his entourage on a hunting trip, a short handscroll by Wang Meng in the Freer.
about: A Manchurian nobleman and his entourage take part in lively activities on a hunting trip in this short handscroll. The movements of the horses, from chasing to catching the quarry, are well shown. The background is painted in the manner of the late Ming landscape master Lan Ying, an unusual mix of the men-and-horses genre with the later landscape tradition. The museum says this may suggest that more than one hand worked on it.

meta: Yun Shouping's Herbaceous Peony of 1685, a withered flower that stands for a lost past in a coded Ming loyalist picture.
about: Yun Shouping came from Piling, modern Changzhou, a center of flower, plant and insect painting. He joined the anti-Manchu resistance, was briefly imprisoned, and saw family members die in 1644. Like other artists he voiced his loyalty to the Ming in coded pictures. The peony, king of flowers, and the spring garden motif took on new meaning under the Qing, and the inscription shows Yun turning the flower into a symbol of the glorious past. The herbaceous peonies here look somewhat withered and pale.
credit_line: Gift of the American Foundation for the Maud E. and Warren H. Corning Botanical Collection
